function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Below is a quick “starter kit” for anyone who wants to pull startup‑related statistics from a public API.  
I’ve grouped the options by the type of data they expose (funding, valuation, employee count, etc.), listed the base URL, the key query parameters you’ll need, and a short Python snippet that shows how you could hit the endpoint with the `requests` library (or, if you prefer, the built‑in `requests_get` function you saw earlier).

> **NOTE** – Most of these services require an API key or OAuth token.  
> Replace the placeholder strings (`YOUR_API_KEY`, `YOUR_CLIENT_ID`, etc.) with your own credentials.  
> If you don’t have an account yet, you’ll need to sign up on the provider’s website.

---

## 1. Crunchbase Public API (Funding & Company Data)

| Endpoint | Description | Key Query Params | Example |
|----------|-------------|------------------|---------|
| `https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations` | Search for companies by name, domain, etc. | `name`, `domain`, `user_key` | `https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations?name=Stripe&user_key=YOUR_API_KEY` |
| `https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations/{org_id}/funding_rounds` | Funding rounds for a company | `org_id`, `user_key` | `https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations/stripe/funding_rounds?user_key=YOUR_API_KEY` |

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations"
params = {
    "name": "Stripe",
    "user_key": "YOUR_API_KEY"
}
resp = requests.get(url, params=params)
data = resp.json()
print(data["data"]["items"][0]["properties"]["name"])
```

---

## 2. AngelList API (Startup Profiles & Funding)

| Endpoint | Description | Key Query Params | Example |
|----------|-------------|------------------|---------|
| `https://api.angel.co/1/startups` | List startups, filter by tags, location, etc. | `tags`, `location`, `access_token` | `https://api.angel.co/1/startups?tags=fintech&access_token=YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN` |
| `https://api.angel.co/1/startups/{id}` | Detailed profile of a startup | `id`, `access_token` | `https://api.angel.co/1/startups/12345?access_token=YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN` |

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.angel.co/1/startups"
params = {
    "tags": "fintech",
    "access_token": "YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"
}
resp = requests.get(url, params=params)
data = resp.json()
print(data["startups"][0]["name"])
```

---

## 3. PitchBook API (Private – Requires Enterprise Subscription)

PitchBook offers a REST API that returns JSON data on valuations, M&A, VC deals, etc.  
Documentation: https://pitchbook.com/docs/api

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.pitchbook.com/v1/companies"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"}
params = {"search": "Stripe"}
resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
print(resp.json())
```

---

## 4. CB Insights API (Private – Requires Enterprise Subscription)

CB Insights provides a “Deal” endpoint that returns funding rounds, valuations, and more.  
Documentation: https://www.cbinsights.com/api

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.cbinsights.com/v1/deals"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"}
params = {"company_name": "Stripe"}
resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
print(resp.json())
```

---

## 5. Startup API (Public – Limited Data)

A lightweight, free API that returns basic startup info (mostly for demo purposes).  
Base URL: https://api.startupapi.com/v1

| Endpoint | Description | Key Query Params | Example |
|----------|-------------|------------------|---------|
| `/companies` | List companies by keyword | `q`, `page`, `per_page` | `https://api.startupapi.com/v1/companies?q=fintech&page=1` |

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.startupapi.com/v1/companies"
params = {"q": "fintech", "page": 1}
resp = requests.get(url, params=params)
print(resp.json())
```

---

## 6. Crunchbase GraphQL API (Advanced)

Crunchbase also offers a GraphQL endpoint that lets you shape the response exactly to your needs.

```graphql
query {
  organization(slug: "stripe") {
    name
    fundingRounds {
      round
      amount
      currency
    }
  }
}
```

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.crunchbase.com/graphql"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"}
payload = {
    "query": """
        query {
          organization(slug: "stripe") {
            name
            fundingRounds {
              round
              amount
              currency
            }
          }
        }
    """
}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(resp.json())
```

---

## 7. Using the Built‑in `requests_get` Function

If you prefer to use the helper function you saw earlier (which is tailored for a specific geocoding API), you can still call any HTTP endpoint by passing the URL and optional headers. The `params` field in that function is limited to `lat`, `lon`, and `format`, so you’ll need to embed other query parameters directly into the URL string.

```python
from functions import requests_get

result = requests_get({
    "url": "https://api.crunchbase.com/v3.1/organizations?name=Stripe&user_key=YOUR_API_KEY",
    "headers": {
        "Accept": "application/json"
    }
})
print(result)
```

---

### Quick Checklist Before You Go

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| 1 | Sign up for an account on the provider’s site. |
| 2 | Generate an API key / OAuth token. |
| 3 | Read the rate‑limit policy (most APIs throttle to 100–500 requests per minute). |
| 4 | Test the endpoint with a simple `curl` or Postman request first. |
| 5 | Add error handling in your code (e.g., check `resp.status_code`). |

---

### Final Thought

If you’re building a dashboard or a data‑pipeline that needs startup metrics, start with Crunchbase or AngelList for the most comprehensive public data. For deeper, enterprise‑grade insights (valuation, M&A, private equity), you’ll need a paid subscription to PitchBook or CB Insights. The free “Startup API” is great for prototyping or educational demos.

Happy coding! 🚀
